title: Grandfather's Dominican roots and descent from Dominique You
summary: Albert traces the Dominique name to the Dominican Republic and a pirate ancestor, discusses why elders avoid family history, and mentions the ancestor's grave.

blocks.x: From what we understand and what we know from the Dominican Republic, derived the name Dominic Cutter-Hugh off of it. And I understand that his grandfather was Dominic Hugh, the pirate on the gene defense ship. Which is all authentic, because there's a lady died here just a few years ago. That was a close cousin, Miss Tomatis, and she told me about my grandfather's grandfather. How do you spell Tomatis? T-O-T-H-O-M-A-T-I-S.
I never heard of that name before. So they came up from the Dominican Republic?

Dominican Republic, as far as I can go back. I try to search my family tree when I come here, but there's not too many of the old relatives here that can sit down, and they don't want to discuss it. There's a lot of it, they claim it's shady background, to me it's not shady. It's just the way that these old people carried themselves in an aristocratic way, even though they were poor, poor people. And their heritage was rich, and their retainer is such. And they don't want to discuss with the youngsters about their family tree. But I do have a lot of information that was given to them.

Well, you know, it always struck me that so many people here came up from maybe in the Dominican Republic, Santa Domingo, whatever you want to call it. That's right, that's right. The revolution down there sent so many people to various places, they ended up in New Orleans.

Well, yes, but not only the revolution, the New World, the dreams of what was in the New World brought these diverse people over here. And naturally, Dominic, you being a part of the piracy days on the ship's ride, I imagine he would leave his family alone, his family's, to meet him around in that way ever he was going to be.

He's buried in the second graveyard on St. Louis in Claymore. It's a little grave there. He has a marker on it. Someone takes care of it, but I don't know who. It's always spotless. But I think it's the Masons. He was a Mason.
